lead.t: Biliary colic: pain caused by a stone temporarily obstructing the cystic duct (or common bile duct).
lead.s: Gallstones: Biliary Colic, Cholecystitis, Cholangitis and Cholecystectomy

b: Severe, steady (not truly colicky) pain that starts abruptly in the epigastrium or right upper quadrant , often after a fatty meal (or at night), builds up for 15 to 60 minutes and lasts 1 to 5 hours , then settles slowly (the stone falls b
Nausea, vomiting, sweating and restlessness (the patient writhes).
Examination between and during attacks: mild epigastric tenderness only, no Murphy's sign , normal temperature and tests.

snip.t: | Gallstone disease / biliary colic | RUQ pain, post‑prandial, radiates to right shoulder | Ultrasound shows stones, liver function tests abnormal |
Look‑alike conditions: functional dyspepsia, gastro‑oesophageal reflux disease, gastric cancer, pancreatitis, biliary colic.
| Biliary colic / choledocholithiasis | Post‑prandial RUQ pain, jaundice, CBD stones on US | Intermittent pain, normal pancreatic enzymes unless pancreatitis co‑exists |
Look‑alike conditions: duodenal ulcer perforation, biliary colic, mesenteric ischemia, acute cholecystitis.
Gallstones (pigment): Chronic bilirubin excess — Biliary colic, cholangitis; ultrasound screening in chronic hemolysis
The spectrum: asymptomatic stones (up to 90% of people with gallstones never have symptoms), biliary colic, cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, cholangitis and pancreatitis.
